MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 22, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:00 p.m., on January 8, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 3, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Liability Claims; Claimants: Noval, Donaldson, Orloff and Gray; Agency Claimed
Against – City of Mission Viejo and; Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to
Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (4 cases)

CS2. Conference with legal Counsel: Pending Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v. The
City of Mission Viejo.

CS3. Conference with legal Counsel: Present Adjudication Pursuant to Section 54956.9 (d1)
- Status Update on Resolution of Issues Matter.

City Council Minutes  1  January 22, 2019
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed three matters in Closed
Session, all dealing with various forms of litigation. The Council received updates and information
but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Raths

PRESENTATIONS

1.  Recognize the 2018 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Raths presented plaques to (1) Environmental Program Administrator, Denise
  Matson, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Firefighter, Kyle Tenney,
  Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year; and (3) Deputy, Dana Chaney,
  Orange County Sheriff’s Department Employee of the Year.

2.  Featured Businesses of the Month - Coastal Naturopathic Wellness and Maggie’s ’76
  Jahroumi Oil Inc.

  Mayor Raths presented proclamations to the owner of Coastal Naturopathic Wellness, Jan
  Eisenbeisz, and Maggie's '76 Jahroumi Oil Inc., Maggie Jahroumi.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Christopher Palacios, Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Explorer and Cadet: thanked
the City for its support of the OCSD/Mission Viejo Explorer program.

Robert Breton, M.V.: announced that he will be making a special presentation on Mission Viejo's
past, present and future at 3:00 p.m. on Sunday, January 27, 2019, in the City Council Chamber.

Ryan Reza Farsai, M.V.: stated that the country's election process is flawed and he has been
traveling up and down the states, asking different cities how they conduct themselves.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 10 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  2  January 22, 2019
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of January 8, 2019, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated December 14, 2018 in the Amount of $1,155,245.84

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated December 21, 2018 in the Amount of $4,612,121.93

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated January 4, 2019 in the Amount of $755,996.28

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2018

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for November 2018

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  November 2018

  Received and filed.

9.  Project W Grant Application—Los Alisos/Santa Margarita Parkway Bus Stop
  Improvements

  Adopted Resolution 19-02 Approving the Submittal of an Application to the Orange
  County Transportation Authority for Funding Under The Measure M2 Project W Program
  for Safe Transit Stops.

10.  Angled Parking and On-Street Parking Modifications on Via Fabricante and Obrero

City Council Minutes  3  January 22, 2019
   (1) Introduced Ordinance 19-327 Authorizing Angled Parking on all Roadways with
  Conditions for Implementation (Mission Viejo Municipal Code Title 14, Chapter 14.01,
  Division 8); and (2) directed staff to return to City Council within 6 months following the
  initial implementation of angled parking on Via Fabricante with recommendations to
  preserve, modify or eliminate said angled parking as appropriate.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

10.  Angled Parking and On-Street Parking Modifications on Via Fabricante and Obrero

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Randy Holbrook, M.V.: stated that he has witnessed traffic and growth in the area but he
  is concerned with the idea of angled parking because traffic on Fabricante consists of
  oversized buses, commercial and delivery trucks, and tow trucks. Mr. Holbrook said that
  backing out of an angled parking space could be a safety issue.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  introduce Ordinance 19-327 Authorizing Angled Parking on all Roadways with
  Conditions for Implementation (Mission Viejo Municipal Code Title 14, Chapter 14.01,
  Division 8); and (2) direct staff to return to City Council within 6 months following the
  initial implementation of angled parking on Via Fabricante with recommendations to
  preserve, modify or eliminate said angled parking as appropriate.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  City Attorney Curley read the Ordinance title for the record.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum congratulated the three employees of the year who were recognized
earlier in the evening. She said that the City’s honoree, Denise Matson, has been a tireless
volunteer and very active in community events. Not only is she a terrific and involved employee
but Denise exemplifies what Mission Viejo is all about as was evident when she thanked the people
she works with. Council Member Bucknum noted that Mission Viejo’s staff do an amazing job
City Council Minutes  4  January 22, 2019
 working together and finding creative solutions that don't cost the taxpayers money. She said
leadership starts at the top so she thanked the City Manager for his stellar management. Council
Member Bucknum congratulated Firefighter Tenney and said it was nice to see his family in the
audience and she enjoyed the humorous jabbing that goes on between the Fire and Sheriff's
departments. She also thanked Deputy Dana Chaney for the very innovative work she is doing
with the homeless. Again, starting at the top with the Chief, she said Lieutenant Vuong is listening
to what the residents are asking for and implementing those things in a creative way. In conclusion,
Council Member Bucknum encouraged residents to attend Robert Breton's history presentation on
Sunday, January 27, 2019, at 3:00 p.m.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced an upcoming blood drive on January 24, 2019, from 12:00 to
6:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. She recommended that residents make an
appointment online at redcrossblood.org (code COMV) or walk in and donate. She stated that this is
the time of year when parents are starting to think about the next school year and where their kids
will go. Council Member Kelley shared that Viejo Elementary is a unique school because it has a
two-way Spanish language immersion program and by 2nd and 3rd grade, most students are fluently
speaking both languages. She noted that tours are offered on Wednesdays and those interested can
contact the school for additional information. Council Member Kelley discussed the issue of San
Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E) electricity rates and announced that two of the issues that are
concerning to residents are moving forward. She said she has learned that SDG&E has petitioned
the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to ask for the high usage charge to be eliminated
and that SDG&E is also studying a change to the climate zone for the area. Council Member Kelley
encouraged residents to contact the CPUC to express their opinions by emailing
public.advisor@cpuc.ca.gov. She reminded residents that customers can also visit the SDG&E
website and ask to have their payments equalized throughout the year. Council Member Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word of the month is perseverance and she thanked Sir
Speedy Printing for donating 1,000 of the character program posters per month for almost 15 years.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs outlined the League of California Cities conference in Sacramento where
he attended the Revenue and Taxation Policy Committee meeting. He reported that taxes are going
up and there is not a lot anyone can do about it. He touched on other topics that were covered at
the conference including affordable housing and tax credits, cities’ loss of control over cannabis
deliveries in their jurisdictions, the PG&E bankruptcy, sales tax revenue for goods ordered online,
and water issues in the State. Council Member Sachs said he learned that 1% of California
taxpayers pay 70% of the General revenue and that Prop 13 may be eliminated for commercial
properties. Referring to Mission Viejo’s recent town hall meeting on skyrocketing electricity rates,
Council Member Sachs said that SDG&E representatives stated that switching rates from coastal
to inland area would not amount to a whole lot of money. He said the idea that SDG&E is going
to the CPUC to seek changes is just a way for them to tell everyone that they tried to do something
but nothing happened.

City Attorney Bill Curley noted that the League of California Cities Attorney group is talking
about soliciting a group of cities to challenge the State over the new cannabis regulations that
Council Member Sachs referred to.

City Council Minutes  5  January 22, 2019
 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell discussed his attendance at a meeting with Assistant City Manager Rattay
and some of the citizens who requested that the City explore Community Choice Aggregate (CCA)
for electric services. He said it was an interesting discussion and it seems to be emerging that there
are choices for buying electricity. Although it would still be delivered by SDG&E or SCE, there
are options for buying electricity from a greener source or one that that may be less expensive. He
noted that it is more complicated than everyone knew at the outset and it would probably take a
consortium of cities working together for the economy of scale to make it work. Mayor Pro Tem
Goodell shared that the Association of California Cities-Orange County is taking a leadership role
in a lot of important issues including homelessness. He said he will be leaving for Washington DC
for a series advocacy meetings that will cover labor law, water delivery and quality, and
homelessness. The City’s new Congressional representative, Katie Porter, will also meet with the
group and more than 30 elected officials from City Councils across Orange County are attending
the conference. Council Member Goodell announced that tomorrow’s Olympic Promotion
Committee meeting will cover a number of opportunities that are coming forward this year
including significant, international dive and swim events at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths outlined his attendance at the Laguna Hills Chamber of Commerce meeting where
Mayor Dore Gilbert gave the State of the City presentation. Mr. Gilbert discussed the Five Lagunas
project on El Toro Road and said it will be at least two to three years before anything is done with
the former Laguna Hills Mall property. Mayor Raths further outlined his attendance at the South
Orange County Association of Mayors breakfast in Irvine. The group received a briefing on what
is happening with the Great Park and the Veterans Cemetery, which may be situated on Great Park
property. He thanked Irvine Mayor Don Wagner for hosting the event. In conclusion, Mayor Raths
announced that the City received a great letter from a private detective who complimented the
Carl's Jr. restaurant on Oso Parkway. The detective wrote the owner about his positive visit, the
cleanliness of the restaurant and a stellar employee who seemed very proud to work there.

12.  Appointment of Mission Viejo City Ambassador

  Mayor Raths presented his agenda report.

  The following expressed their concern with the proposed City Ambassador position and
  the nominee, Dave Leckness: Cathy Schlicht, M.V. and Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 19-03 Establishing the Role of City Ambassador, Pursuant to Mission
  Viejo Municipal Code Section 2.04.040; and (2) authorize the Mayor to appoint the 2019
  City Ambassador.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley and Raths
  NOES:  Goodell and Sachs
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  January 22, 2019
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:05 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 12, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.
